chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his father (peace be upon him), from Jabir ibn Abdullah Al-Ansari, who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who pleases a ruling authority by angering Allah, exits from the religion of Allah.'
ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of pleasing a ruler by angering God?
ai.summary: In Shia political theology, this hadith from al-Kafi establishes a critical criterion for religious integrity: obedience to temporal authority is conditional upon its alignment with divine will. It underscores the principle of 'exit from religion' (kharaja min dīn Allāh) not merely as apostasy, but as a forfeiture of faith when one prioritizes the satisfaction of rulers over God's commands, a concept central to the legitimacy of the Imamate and the status of the righteous in times of political oppression.
